newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha remains above $200 in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha remains above $200 in thin trade.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were virtually unchanged on Tuesday in slim trade with most dealers attending an industry conference in Singapore, traders said.
Trading is expected to remain quiet until next Tuesday as the Tokyo market will be closed on Monday for a national holiday, they added.
Bids for second-half November open-spec naphtha were assessed at $200.00, with offers at $201.00. On Monday, it changed hands at $201.00.
First-half November was quoted around 50 cents higher than the second-half November level.
In middle distillates, refiners are carefully considering when to raise kerosene yields at the expense of gas oil production to build up kerosene stockpiles for winter, traders said.
Most refiners are likely to start shifting from maximum gas oil production to maximum kerosene output in the second half of October or early November, they said.

Low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) trading was lacklustre as mild weather depressed demand from power firms. Indonesian cargoes were notionally assessed at about 60 cents above the Pertamina formula. --Tokyo Commodities (81-3 3432 8837)
